subject: HIPAA residency & add-on fee structuring — implementation credit vs recurring
messages:
From: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@medwell.ai>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@medwell.ai
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify HIPAA residency + addon fees for pilot (SOW attached)

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team liked the latency guarantees. Procurement asked me to follow up with a clearer breakdown for the HIPAA/residency work we discussed. Specifically they want: 

- One-time implementation/attestation work (estimated effort & recommended crediting approach)
- Ongoing residency fee (audit log retention + regional egress) vs. a per-seat HSM/KMS license
- Option that minimizes cash up-front for our pilot (6 months) but that lets us scale later

I've attached the SOW draft with the technical scope and a rough install calendar. Our internal budget for Q3 is tight so if there's a path that avoids a large upfront invoice that's ideal.

Can you send a simple pricing split (2-3 options) and call out what you would amortize vs bill monthly? Also please flag any evidence deliverables we should expect.

Appreciate it —
Sara
Procurement, MedWell Health

Attachments: MedWell_SOW_draft_v2.pdf (pdf)
From: markus_klein@redwood.ai <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@medwell.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 12:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Clarify HIPAA residency + addon fees for pilot (SOW attached)

Sara —

Thanks for the SOW and the clear asks. Quick initial read: scope looks standard and we can structure 3 clean options to match MedWell's risk posture and budget cadence. I'll outline them below and attach a one-page workback.

Option A (Low upfront / higher recurring):
- Implementation: covered as a monthly credit across first 6 months (we amortize the implementation cost into a reduced monthly residency fee).
- Residency fee: $X/month (includes audit log retention 2y, 24/7 logging ingestion, regional egress up to 5TB/mo).
- HSM/KMS: charged as per-tenant usage ($0.XX per HSM-op) with a small per-seat admin surcharge.

Option B (Balanced):
- Implementation: 50% upfront invoice, 50% amortized over 12 months as a credit.
- Residency fee: lower than A (since partial upfront), audit log retention configurable to 7 years at additional tiered cost.
- HSM/KMS: offer 'seat' licensing for pilot (2 admin seats) at a fixed monthly seat rate to simplify procurement.

Option C (Upfront-capex friendly):
- Implementation: one-time invoice (discounted) but minimal recurring residency fee.
- Residency fee: minimal if you commit to a 12-month minimum.
- HSM/KMS: on-prem HSM seat purchase option (upfront) + discounted ops fees.

Evidence & deliverables: audit log export cadence (monthly), SOC2-lite attestation for pilot, KMS attestation doc, and invoice schedule. If legal needs a schedule for evidence delivery, we can include a milestone table (we suggested in SOW).

Next step: Laura, Ben — could you take the sheet I attached and convert to two finance-friendly line items (implementation credit schedule + recurring SKU mapping)? Sara, if you can confirm which financial team you'll run this by and any PO cadence constraints (quarterly vs annual), we'll tailor the numbers.

Markus Klein
Head of Sales — Compliance & Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachments: pricing_workback.xlsx (xlsx)
From: procurement@medwell.ai <procurement@medwell.ai>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@medwell.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 16:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Clarify HIPAA residency + addon fees for pilot (SOW attached)

Markus —

Thanks for the three options. A couple of clarifying points from our side: 

1) Our CFO prefers minimal capex in Q3 and we'd rather keep pilot payments on Opex. Option A is closest to that, but we need a max monthly cap — we can't expose to unbounded egress spikes. Can you add a clear overage rate and an optional soft cap (e.g., 5TB included, then fixed block pricing)?

2) For HSM/KMS, legal asked whether a seat-license model could be converted to usage-based later without penalty. We need a clear downgrade/upgrade path in the contract.

3) Finally, can you provide a sample invoice schedule that shows: initial invoice (if any), monthly credit offsets, and the first 3 months of billing reconciliation so procurement can map to our GL.

We're targeting a signature by end of July for the pilot start on Aug 15.

Regards,
MedWell Procurement Team

Attachments: none
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: procurement@medwell.ai, Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@medwell.ai>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 20:05:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Clarify HIPAA residency + addon fees for pilot (SOW attached)

Hi Sara / Procurement —

Appreciate the constraints — we can absolutely make Option A procurement-friendly. A few commitments we will include in the commercial terms: 

- Soft cap block: first 5TB of egress included / additional blocks of 1TB at $Y per block. We will also include an optional monthly hard cap with a negotiated throttling-fallback to prevent surprise costs.
- HSM/KMS conversion: seat-to-usage conversion allowed at any time with an immediate pro-rated credit for the remaining seat months. No penalty for conversion during the pilot.
- Invoice schedule (sample):
  * Month 0 (setup): $0 (implementation fully amortized as credit across months 1-6)
  * Month 1-3: residency fee minus amortized credit line item (see attached sample invoice rows)
  * Reconciliation: we provide monthly usage statements and a 30-day reconciliation window; any overage billed following reconciliation.

I'll attach the invoice sample and revised pricing sheet to the HubSpot deal so procurement can pull line items directly. If this looks good we'll update the SOW to explicitly note the amortization and the conversion mechanics and send a redline to legal.

Ben — could you confirm the exact per-block overage number and add the soft cap fallback verbiage?

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Pricing & Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: pricing_workback.xlsx (updated) (xlsx), sample_invoice_rows.csv (csv)
